subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic Feishu group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The requested behavior creates durable agents, workspaces, configs, skills, memory namespaces, and message-routing authority from group-chat sender identities, which automation cannot safely choose without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design generic contract first
options.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel-owned surface.

options.title: Keep session-only routing
options.body: Keep current `groupSessionScope` and explicit subagent/thread mechanisms, documenting that full per-user agent orchestration belongs in external deployment patterns for now.

options.title: Reject automatic provisioning
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers decide group identities should not create durable OpenClaw agents automatically.

recommendation.title: Design generic contract first
recommendation.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel-owned surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent checked-in Feishu routing, dynamic-agent, and subagent-hook history points to steipete, making him the best available owner for the product/security shape decision.
